title: Engineering Manager -Backend
content:
About Meesho 
 
Mission and Vision 
 
Meesho is India’s fastest-growing internet commerce company, driven by the mission to democratize internet commerce for everyone (DICE). Our vision is to enable 100 million small businesses and entrepreneurs in India to succeed online, making online commerce accessible to all. This core purpose guides us in empowering sellers across the country and bringing a diverse range of products to first-time internet shoppers. By leveraging technology and a unique zero commission model, Meesho has opened the doors of e-commerce to millions who were previously underserved. 
 
Technological Scale & Innovation
 
 At Meesho, technology is at the heart of our success. We have invested in a scalable infrastructure and innovative solutions to meet the demands of a vast user base and complex marketplace. Some key highlights include: 
 
Massive Scale: Our backend systems handle millions of orders per day from across India, reaching about 5% of all Indian households, all with near-zero downtime to date. Achieving this level of reliability and performance in a hyper-growth environment is a testament to our engineering excellence. 
 
 Marketplace Reach: Over 1.75 million sellers are registered on Meesho’s platform, supported by our state-of-the-art tech infrastructure and pan-India logistics network. This wide reach — covering virtually every serviceable pin code in the country — presents unique engineering challenges in areas like search, personalization, and payments at scale.
 
 Scalable Architecture: We continually innovate our architecture for growth.. Our quest to serve a billion Indian users has helped us evolve our technologies from a monolith to microservices to now a high scale federated architecture. This evolution allows us to build and deploy features rapidly while maintaining stability for a fast-growing user base. 
 
Cutting-edge Tech Stack: Our platform is built using modern, open-source technologies on the cloud while ensuring high efficiency. We strategically choose proven tools (for example, Java and Golang for services, Kafka for messaging, Dragonfly and Redis for caching, ScyllaDB, MySQL and Mongo for Data) and leverage GCP infrastructure to ensure high performance, reliability, and flexibility. By focusing on the right tools for the right problems, we innovate pragmatically rather than chasing every new tech hype, which helps us solve real-world problems effectively. 
 
Engineering Culture & Challenges 
 
Engineering at Meesho is driven by a bold and inclusive culture that values innovation, ownership, and continuous improvement. We believe that building great products goes hand-in-hand with building a great team. Key aspects of our engineering culture include: 
 
Long Term Thinking: We believe in thinking for tomorrow while building for today, this approach has helped us not only to handle and evolve for scale but also focus on extensibility and stability by investing in the platform
 
Lightspeed: We prioritize rapid iteration and delivery. Engineers are encouraged to ship fast and refine continuously, as we value in order to learn and adapt quickly. 
 
Continuous Improvement: We view failures and bugs as opportunities to improve. A blameless post-mortem culture ensures that mistakes become lessons, fostering an environment where learning from failure drives resilience and innovation.
 
 Ownership Mindset: Every engineer is empowered to act like an owner. We instill a “Founder’s Mindset,” encouraging engineers to take end-to-end ownership of projects and drive them with an entrepreneurial spirit. This means our teams proactively identify problems and champion solutions, just as a founder would for their own product. 
 
Engineering at Meesho is more than just writing code – it's about solving complex, impactful problems at an unprecedented scale. Our engineers tackle challenging use cases (from enabling real-time logistics across India to optimizing a vast product catalog for the next billion users), making a tangible impact on millions of entrepreneurs and customers. We maintain a
professional, yet passionate work environment where the drive to innovate is balanced with a pragmatic approach to problem-solving. 
 
About the Role
 
We are looking for Engineering Manager well-versed with emerging technologies to join our team.
 As an Engineering Manager, you will ensure consistency and quality by shaping the right strategies. You will keep an eye on all engineering projects and ensure all duties are fulfilled . You will analyse other employees’ tasks and carry on collaborations effectively. You will also transform newbies into experts and build reports on the progress of all projects.

title: Manager – GTM & Sales Strategy, Meesho AI Services (MAS)
content:
About the Team
MAS's mission is to accelerate the build and deployment of an AI workforce for every business — from kirana to conglomerate. Our vision is to deliver a billion-plus workflows through our agents in ways that drive real client outcomes, not automation for its own sake.
We go deep rather than wide. Today that means known, process-defined, repeatable service workflows — inbound contact-centre work (calls, chats, tickets), plus the outbound work that behaves like a cost workflow rather than a conversion one (lead qualification and verification, not lead conversion) — anywhere we can benchmark against a cost line the client already feels, guarantee savings, and hold the quality bar. We're deliberately building a technology company, not an AI BPO: models are a commodity, so our moat is the workflow knowledge, integrations, and client relationships that only come from actually running the work — not a generic AI layer bolted onto a call centre.
We've proven this model works — with marquee clients across consumer durables, auto, and D2C/marketplace businesses — and we're still early. We'll keep evolving it as we go, staying client-first rather than assuming we already have the answer. This is a 0–1 business inside Meesho: no fixed playbook, high ownership, and the ground floor of how India's enterprises adopt AI-led operations.
About the Role
This role is for a GTM generalist who thrives in ambiguity, is genuinely excited about AI-led offerings, and wants to build the full range of enterprise sales skills — with an eye on growing into a closer and sales leader over time, or moving into Business/GTM Operations. Both are real paths from this seat.
You own the middle mile of the deal: the stretch between a qualified conversation and a close-ready opportunity. That means deep client discovery, mapping who really decides, understanding how a client's teams actually work today, and making sure the deal never goes cold on your watch — following up, keeping momentum, and setting up the closer to walk into the room fully briefed. Our central team owns top-of-funnel lead-gen, but this isn't a purely inbound or coordination role — you'll still make cold calls and run early client meetings yourself when a deal needs it.
A lot of enterprise AI-services deals across this market stall before signature for a simple reason: nobody on the deal ever gets deep enough into the account to know what the client is actually buying, or who really decides. That's exactly the gap this role exists to close — the middle mile is where deals live or die.

Your mission is to ensure near-zero vulnerabilities from application and data security failures reach production. A significant portion of your focus will involve advanced Red Teaming, utilizing LLMs to improve Meesho's security posture, and architecting defenses for our autonomous AI systems against prompt injection, data leakage, and jailbreaking attacks.

title: AI Product Engineer
content:
Role Overview
We are transitioning our organization to an AI-first operational model. We are seeking an AI Product Engineer to architect and build the company’s central intelligence engine.
In this role, you will be the primary builder of automated intelligence systems—tools that not only retrieve insights but actively trigger workflows, and synthesize strategic intel across our entire business landscape.
Role Profile
This is a high-impact, hands-on engineering role requiring a convergence of three distinct skill sets:
Software Engineering (50%): Building scalable middleware, API integrations, and production-grade applications that connect our data stack to business tools (CRM, Marketing Automation, Support/Ticketing).
AI Engineering (30%): Implementing Agentic workflows, RAG architectures, and LLMs to process unstructured data at scale.
Data Analytics (20%): Leveraging SQL and B2B SaaS metrics to ensure all automation is grounded in accurate, governed data.
Key Responsibilities
1. Building the "Enterprise Brain" (Architecture & Integration)
Develop a unified intelligence layer that ingests signals from disparate sources (Product Telemetry, CRM, Call Transcripts, Marketing inputs) and processes them into actionable outputs.
Build robust integrations/webhooks to push AI-generated insights directly into workflow tools (e.g., pushing "Churn Risk" alerts into Salesforce
2. AI Logic & Agent Implementation
Architect "Agentic" workflows where LLMs are granted permission to perform tasks 
Implement advanced RAG to ground AI outputs in company documentation, historical data, and strategic context.
Ensure rigorous evaluation and guardrails for non-deterministic models to prevent "hallucinations" in critical business workflows.
3. Data Engineering & Governance
Collaborate with Analytics Engineers to ensure the underlying data pipelines support real-time or near-real-time AI applications.
Maintain security and privacy standards, ensuring that AI agents respect data access permissions across different departments.
Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications:
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
Software Engineering: 3+ years of experience in Python development, with strong proficiency in API development (FastAPI/Django) and building integrations between SaaS platforms.
AI/ML Application: Proven experience building applications using LLM APIs and orchestration frameworks, Experience with "Agent" concepts.
Data Proficiency: Strong SQL skills and familiarity with cloud data warehouses (Snowflake/BigQuery).
Preferred Qualifications:
Business Systems Knowledge: Experience working with APIs for major B2B tools (Salesforce, HubSpot, Zendesk, Jira, Marketo).
Workflow Automation: Experience with tools like Airflow, Zapier/Make (advanced usage), or custom workflow engines.
B2B Domain Expertise: Understanding of the interplay between Sales, Product, and Customer Success.
Competencies
The "Builder" Mindset: You are comfortable taking a high-level strategic requirement from leadership (e.g., "We need to automate lead qualification") and independently architecting and coding the solution.
Systemic Thinking: You understand how a change in product data schema impacts the downstream marketing automation flow.
Adaptability: You can switch contexts rapidly—from debugging a SQL query for Strategy to refining a prompt for Customer Support automation.

Job Snapshot
A revenue manager runs a business through people. Every week they choose where their limited attention goes: which deal to step into, who on the team needs coaching, which problem to leave alone. An hour spent rescuing one account is an hour not spent developing a rep. The information needed to choose well already exists, but it sits scattered across the CRM, recorded calls, dashboards, and enablement tools, and managers assemble it by hand.
Mindtickle is building Manager Effectiveness, the product charter that owns that choice. It helps revenue managers and leaders direct scarce management attention toward the interventions that matter most across the business and the people they are responsible for.
We need a Group Product Manager to own it. The problem is hard in a specific way: "where should this manager spend their next hour?" has no correct answer sitting in a table, and the products render judgments about people that a manager or a CFO will challenge. You will decide what counts as correct, get customers to agree with it, and defend it. You will have no reports and the full charter: product direction, roadmap, customer relationships, pricing, and revenue.

Role summary
The Program Manager, Services runs the internal programs that make Mindtickle Services efficient, predictable and profitable. The role spans all four service lines — Professional Services, Content as a Service (CaaS), Managed Services and Technical Solutions — rather than a single customer engagement.
You will own portfolio-wide visibility into cost, revenue, margin and sourcing (in-house vs. outsourced); run strategic Services initiatives from charter to closure; coordinate internal response on escalations and accounts that need operational support; and build the executive narratives that leadership uses with founders, Sales and customers.
This is a hands-on, high-ownership role for a structured operator who is equally comfortable in a spreadsheet, a platform, a cross-functional working session and an executive deck.
 
Key responsibilities
1) Services portfolio governance & visibility
Build and maintain a single source of truth across PS, CaaS, Managed Services and Technical Solutions: active programs, capacity, utilization, delivery health and risk.
Run the Services governance cadence — weekly portfolio reviews, monthly business reviews and quarterly planning — with clear decision logs and action tracking.
Define and standardize portfolio metrics and reporting so leadership can see issues early and act on data, not anecdotes.
2) Program financials: cost, revenue & sourcing
Track Services revenue, cost and margin by service line, account and program; surface variance and its drivers.
Maintain clear visibility into what is delivered in-house versus outsourced — vendor spend, contractor utilization and the cost/quality trade-off of each.
Support pricing, estimation and capacity models with leadership, Finance and Presales; flag margin risk before deals are signed and during delivery.
Prepare inputs for budgeting, forecasting and headcount planning.
3) Strategic initiatives
Charter, plan and drive Services-wide initiatives end to end — e.g., AI-led delivery transformation, new service packaging, operating-model changes and tooling rollouts.
Own initiative governance: scope, milestones, owners, dependencies, RAID logs and success metrics.
Hold cross-functional owners accountable and report progress and outcomes to leadership.
4) Escalation & account operations support
Act as the program lead on escalations: assemble the right internal team, run the recovery plan, track commitments and close the loop.
Provide operational support to accounts that need it — resourcing gaps, cross-team dependencies, commercial or scope clarity — without becoming the day-to-day delivery owner.
Capture root causes and turn recurring issues into process or product fixes.
5) Operational efficiency & process improvement
Identify inefficiencies across service functions — hand-offs, duplicated effort, tooling gaps, manual reporting — and drive measurable fixes.
Standardize playbooks, templates and operating rhythms across service lines.
Partner with team leads to apply AI and automation to internal workflows (reporting, estimation, resource allocation).
6) Executive communication & storytelling
Build executive presentations for founders, leadership reviews, Sales/GTM forums and customer executive meetings.
Turn operational data into a clear narrative: what is happening, why it matters and what decision is needed.
Draft briefs, business cases and updates for Services leadership.
Tools, cadences & metrics
Tools: Jira, Rocketlane, Excel/Google Sheets, Salesforce (inputs), BI dashboards, Google Slides/PowerPoint, and AI assistants for analysis and drafting.

title: AWS Data Engineer (Senior) (Freelancer)
content:
Mactores is the agent-native AWS modernization firm. Most modernization work doesn't ship, it stalls in pilots, slips a year, or lands at three times the budget. We exist to ship it: production systems running, legacy retired, outcomes measured. Our delivery is built on Aedeon, the agent platform built by Mactores' founders' sister company, which absorbs the repetitive 60–70% of engagement work, discovery, dependency mapping, validation, test generation, that traditional consulting bills human hours against. Forward-deployed engineers own the rest: architecture, judgment, and cutover, on dates we commit to in the contract.


This is a senior freelance role in our Data Platform Modernization pillar: consolidating and migrating customer data infrastructure on AWS in weeks, not quarters. Customers come to us after a data program has stalled — pipelines nobody trusts, warehouses nobody runs new workloads on, a modernization that produced diagrams instead of production systems.
Aedeon handles automated source discovery, schema mapping, lineage extraction, and parallel-run validation. You take the work that needs a senior engineer's judgment: pipeline builds on EMR and Glue, data models for Redshift, Snowflake, Athena, and Presto, Airflow orchestration, and the troubleshooting that gets a system stable enough to cut over. Freelance here means real delivery work on real engagements — not staff augmentation into someone else's backlog.

title: Sr Data Scientist
content:
Nium provides global infrastructure for real-time cross-border payments. We were founded on the mission to deliver the global payments infrastructure of tomorrow, today. Our platform enables banks, fintechs, and global businesses to move money instantly, everywhere.   
Co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore with offices in 14 markets worldwide, we are entering one of the most exciting chapters in our journey. In March 2026, we delivered the largest month in our 11-year history with record revenue, record volumes, and EBITDA profitability. Today, Nium moves nearly $60B in payments annually, almost entirely for enterprises, while continuing to strengthen an already healthy balance sheet.  
It is an incredible time to join us, and we are only just getting started.  
Our payout network spans 190+ countries and 100 currencies, with 100 + corridors in real time. We power seamless transfers to accounts, wallets, and cards, support local collections in 35 markets, and as a principal card issuer on Visa, Mastercard, Discover, and UATP, Nium issues over 50 million card tokens every year. Backed by regulatory licenses in 40+ markets, we make it simple for our partners to onboard, integrate, and scale globally. This scale and innovation have earned us recognition as one of CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies 2025, winner of Best Cross-Border Payments Solution at the PayTech Awards, and inclusion in FXC Intelligence’s Top 100 Cross-Border Payments Companies list.  
In 2024, we raised US$50 million in Series E funding at a US$1.4 billion valuation to accelerate network expansion, product innovation, and talent growth. With the B2B payments market projected to hit US$175 trillion by 2030, Nium offers ambitious builders the chance to shape the future of global money movement with the scale of a leader and the energy of a high-growth company. 


The increasing volume, complexity, and regulatory scrutiny of financial‑crime and compliance risks requires advanced, data‑driven capabilities that traditional analytics and manual processes can no longer support. The Compliance Data Scientist will significantly enhance Nium’s ability to detect emerging risks, optimise controls, meet regulatory expectations, and drive operational efficiency across the compliance function. 
This role fills a critical capability gap and directly supports strategic priorities including automation, risk‑based decisioning, model optimisation, data‑quality improvement, and regulatory assurance. Additionally, this role is specifically designed to support activities related to transitioning compliance systems to advanced, data-driven Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning solutions e.g. Transaction Monitoring detection models. 
Role Summary: 
Responsible for development of AI/ML models to identify risks (such as fraud or credit risk) while ensuring these models are auditable, explainable, and compliant with data privacy laws

title: Design System/UX Engineer
content:
At TTEC Digital, we coach clients to ensure their employees feel valued, and fully supported, because an amazing customer experience is an employee first process. Our vision is the same, a place where employees know they can thrive.

TTEC Digital seeks a Design System/UX Engineer to join our team. This role is a full-time and fully remote opportunity! 
The work:
We’re an innovation group inside TTEC (NASDAQ: TTEC), building the next generation of AI CX tools — automated QA, conversational analytics, knowledge assist, and agentic automation — for the world’s biggest brands and the millions of customers they serve. We move like an early-stage startup, backed by the scale, distribution, and enterprise client base of a company that’s been obsessed with customer experience since 1982. 
This is the rare seat where getting in early actually matters at scale. TTEC is a public company at an AI inflection point. Ship the right products into thousands of live enterprise deployments and you don’t just move a metric — you move the trajectory of the company and the value of the stock. The leverage is real, and the work compounds. 
Who we hire — the DNA:
Self-starters and do-ers with grit — hackers in the best sense, with a startup mentality and a show-me bias: working software over slides, prototypes over proposals. 
Want to learn, love new technology. This platform is built on the latest technology, and that technology changes and advances monthly. You adapt to change quickly — new tools, new models, new priorities — without drama. 
Master debuggers and problem solvers. You love solving complex problems, you think outside the box, and you multitask across domains without losing the thread. 
AI-native. You work with AI on all levels — you understand the technology around you (LLMs, SLMs, RAG, knowledge graphs, agents, training, eval) and you use AI tools daily to exponentially increase your velocity. 
Distributed-systems literate. High-efficiency, event-driven, low-latency systems are our world; you understand what that demands. 
Innovators who ship. You demonstrate ideas easily, fail fast, and move forward. You make committed timelines and hit them. 
You consider yourself exceptional — and you like winning. So do we. 
No one will have everything in this description. We're looking for well-rounded, smart people who move fast.
What You Will Do:
The role:
Own the design system in code and the UX of the wedge — the Agent UI shell, slide-out / pill, Control UI, and the per-module panels.
UX here ships as code, not Figma hand-offs. This is not a look-pretty job: the UI renders live voice, desktop, and AI event streams in real time, and you have to understand the technology underneath — events, WebSocket state, latency, plugin loading — so what you design flows and works, not just looks good.
Startup environment: 1-week sprints, Friday demos, fail fast, move forward. 
What you'll own:
The design system as a real component library — templates and patterns developers implement without friction
Agent UI / Control UI interaction patterns
Active Listening and Agent Handover UX
The graphics language of the product (iconography, motion, data visualization)
Accessibility (Lighthouse a11y > 90) and keyboard-first agent flows
Your committed timelines. 
Who you are:
A self-starter with taste and grit — a designer who ships.
Show-me mentality: you demo working UI on Fridays like every other engineer.
You think from the developer's seat: every component you design, you've already thought through how the squads will implement, extend, and theme it — your design system makes them faster, never slower.
You love new technology, adapt fast when the product shifts weekly, use AI tools daily to multiply velocity, consider yourself exceptional, and like winning. 
What You Will Bring:
7+ years of product design with real front-end engineering — you ship React + TypeScript, not just specs. 
Strong graphics experience — ++++ on visual craft: iconography, motion design, canvas/SVG data visualization, rendering dense live data beautifully and legibly. 
Has owned a design system as a living component library in a fast-shipping product — versioned, documented, themed, adopted. 
Strong templating discipline — reusable patterns and layout systems built for developer implementation; you understand component APIs, composition, and what makes a pattern cheap or expensive to build. 
Understands the tech underneath — WebSocket-driven state, event ordering, render performance, module federation/plugin loading — well enough that your designs never fight the architecture. 
Strong on dense, real-time, professional-tool UX (think trading terminals, not marketing sites) — an agent lives in this UI 8 hours a day. 
Accessibility and keyboard-first design as defaults, not afterthoughts. 
Perceived-performance craft — skeletons, optimistic updates, motion that masks latency; the UI must feel instant even when the network isn't. 
Design tokens as the theming backbone — enterprise customers will want branding; tokens make that config, not a rewrite. 
Overlay/extension constraints fluency — designing UI injected over a host page (pill, slide-out) with its size, z-index, and isolation realities. 
Usability evidence at startup speed — lightweight session recordings and agent feedback loops instead of month-long studies. 
A debugger in the browser — you profile the render, find the jank, and fix your own component.

What You Will Do: 
The role:
Build Desktop Intercept — the native Windows driver and app that acts as a virtual mic/speaker, replaces audio in real time, and (Phase 1 Phase C) reads the DOM and drives Computer Use.
This is the hardest engineering on the platform and the deepest moat. Everything you build feeds a high-efficiency, event-driven, low-latency distributed platform — voice, desktop, intelligence, and AI combined — so you think in latency budgets, throughput, and efficiency, not just features.
Startup environment: 1-week sprints, Friday demos, fail fast and move forward. 
What you'll own:
Windows native driver (WASAPI, virtual audio devices, kernel-adjacent hooks) · real-time bidirectional audio routing
The user-space app (audio router, DOM scraper, MCP server)
The desktop-to-cloud path onto the event bus (NATS-class, WebSocket) under a sub-300ms budget
AV co-existence and mass-deployment
Your committed timelines. 
Who you are:
Self-starter, hacker, grit.
You consider yourself exceptional at the systems level and can show it.
You love new technology, adapt fast when it changes, demonstrate ideas with working code, and use AI tools daily to multiply your velocity.
Team player who makes and hits committed timelines.
Loves solving the problems nobody else can — and winning. 
What You Will Bring:
8+ years systems / native development; shipped a Windows desktop agent at real scale (>10k seats) with audio. 
Strong C/C++ — mandatory. Strong Go for the service side — mandatory. 
Comfortable building and interacting with drivers — virtual audio devices, virtual microphones/speakers, WASAPI / Core Audio, kernel-adjacent hooks. 
Real-time audio pipelines under a sub-300ms budget — buffering, resampling, drift, glitch-free capture/playback. 
Understands high-efficiency systems end-to-end — event-driven architecture, pub/sub, WebSocket streaming, and what state, race conditions, and locking mean at the native layer (lock-free audio buffers, real-time threads, priority inversion). 
macOS / Linux native experience is a huge +++++ — cross-platform desktop is where this goes next. 
Browser / DOM internals and process injection a strong plus (Phase C). 
Enterprise mass-deployment craft — MSI/installer engineering, silent deploys, fleet upgrades across 10k+ locked-down seats. 
Driver/code signing and AV/EDR co-existence — WHQL, EV certs, and staying invisible to CrowdStrike-class agents without tripping them. 
Crash-dump and telemetry discipline — WinDbg/minidumps, symbolized crash reporting from the field; you debug machines you'll never touch. 
Security posture — least-privilege service design; this app hears customer audio and reads screens, so it must be provably tight. 
A master debugger at the systems level — kernel logs, crash dumps, audio glitches, AV interference; you see it. 
SIP / RTP a strong plus. Mid-tier or better hands-on AI-in-product experience a plus (the desktop app hosts an MCP server and drives Computer Use).

title: QA Lead /SDET Lead
content:
At TTEC Digital, we coach clients to ensure their employees feel valued, and fully supported, because an amazing customer experience is an employee first process. Our vision is the same, a place where employees know they can thrive.

TTEC Digital seeks a QA/SDET Lead to join our team. This role is a full-time and fully remote opportunity! 
The work:
We’re an innovation group inside TTEC (NASDAQ: TTEC), building the next generation of AI CX tools — automated QA, conversational analytics, knowledge assist, and agentic automation — for the world’s biggest brands and the millions of customers they serve. We move like an early-stage startup, backed by the scale, distribution, and enterprise client base of a company that’s been obsessed with customer experience since 1982. 
This is the rare seat where getting in early actually matters at scale. TTEC is a public company at an AI inflection point. Ship the right products into thousands of live enterprise deployments and you don’t just move a metric — you move the trajectory of the company and the value of the stock. The leverage is real, and the work compounds. 
Who we hire — the DNA: 
Self-starters and do-ers with grit — hackers in the best sense, with a startup mentality and a show-me bias: working software over slides, prototypes over proposals. 
Want to learn, love new technology. This platform is built on the latest technology, and that technology changes and advances monthly. You adapt to change quickly — new tools, new models, new priorities — without drama. 
Master debuggers and problem solvers. You love solving complex problems, you think outside the box, and you multitask across domains without losing the thread. 
AI-native. You work with AI on all levels — you understand the technology around you (LLMs, SLMs, RAG, knowledge graphs, agents, training, eval) and you use AI tools daily to exponentially increase your velocity. 
Distributed-systems literate. High-efficiency, event-driven, low-latency systems are our world; you understand what that demands. 
Innovators who ship. You demonstrate ideas easily, fail fast, and move forward. You make committed timelines and hit them. 
You consider yourself exceptional — and you like winning. So do we. 
No one will have everything in this description. We're looking for well-rounded, smart people who move fast.
What You Will Do: 
The role:
Automation-first quality engineering for a platform combining voice, desktop, intelligence, and AI.
We emphasize AUTOMATION — we do not do manual QA here.
Weekly code deploys are the heartbeat: when a QA branch is ready, regressions run fast, results report fast, and the train doesn't wait.
Startup environment: 1-week sprints, fail fast, move forward. 
What you'll own:
Quality strategy across the 1-week cadence as surface area grows 
The cross-service contract suite gating production
Future (phase 2) QA hires
Sets the automation patterns by shipping them; raises the QA engineers around you.
Automation coverage for your squads' services
Fast-turnaround regression suites gating weekly deploys
Rapid detection and reporting
Quality signal in minutes, not days
Load/stress coverage for your services' latency budgets 
Your committed timelines.
Who you are: 
Keeps the respect of senior engineers through technical credibility; comfortable telling a tech lead their branch isn't ready — and delivering that fast, with data.
Show-me mentality on committed timelines: quality visible in every Friday demo, never the bottleneck.
Chaos/failure-injection mindset — kill a service, drop the bus, flap the network; prove the platform degrades gracefully. 
Self-starter with grit and a show-me mentality.
You consider yourself exceptional, love new technology, adapt fast when the stack changes under you, and use AI tools daily to multiply velocity — including AI-assisted test generation.
A team player who likes winning, and a partner to dev, not a gate: when something breaks, you help the dev team isolate it fast. 
 What You Will Bring: 
The QA/SDET Lead role builds upon our Senior QA/SDET profile by adding team leadership responsibilities. This is a player-coach position where the individual leads the quality engineering function while remaining hands-on with framework design, automation architecture, and the team's most complex technical challenges.
8+ years QA/SDET; you have built a test-automation foundation from scratch for a fast-shipping product — you'll build ours before scaled module QA exists.  
Master issue-isolator and root-cause debugger — you narrow a failure to the service, the commit, the event; dev teams love your bug reports because they're half the debugging done. 
Fast regression discipline — parallelized suites, smart test selection, results in minutes; quality at weekly-deploy speed without becoming the bottleneck. 
Comfortable in high-load testing environments — load, stress, and soak testing of high-throughput, low-latency systems; you know how to find the knee of the curve. 
Experience testing event-driven systems, WebSocket flows, and browser extensions — ordering, race conditions, real-time state. 
CI-native mindset — tests wired into trunk-based CI/CD; flake management as a first-class discipline (a flaky suite is a broken suite). 
Contract/API testing between services; synthetic data and traffic generation (simulated calls, event streams, audio) for repeatable real-time testing. 
Testing AI outputs — eval-style assertions for non-deterministic LLM/ML features — a strong plus.

CI/CD (trunk-based, daily prod deploys, PR-to-staging)

Observability and monitoring baselines
Uptime as a personal mission
On-call rotation with the SRE
Your committed timelines.

A ways-to-YES engineer — when a squad needs something, your default is "here's how we do it safely," never a block.
Self-starter, grit, show-me mentality: your infra demos too.

Team player who likes winning.

7+ years DevOps / platform; deep GCP plus real multi-cloud experience — you've deployed and run production workloads on at least two clouds and built abstractions that keep us portable. 
Strong INFRA-AS-CODE mentality — Terraform-class IaC is how everything exists; if it isn't in code, it isn't real. Reviewable, repeatable, destroyable, rebuildable. 
Has run infra for a daily-deploy, trunk-based shop; CI/CD for high-cadence teams is muscle memory. 
Codes — Go or Python tooling, not just YAML. 
Good networking understanding — protocols and how they actually work: TCP/UDP, TLS, HTTP/2, WebSocket, DNS, load balancing, and ideally RTP/SIP for our media paths. You debug at the packet level when you have to.

GitOps discipline — desired state in git, drift detection, PR-driven infra change. 
Deploy safety engineering — canary/progressive rollout, feature-flag integration, instant rollback; weekly deploys stay boring. 
Kubernetes/container depth (GKE-class) — scheduling, autoscaling, resource tuning for latency-sensitive services. 
Secrets and least-privilege IAM as defaults; SOC 2-ready posture without slowing the train. 
Cost awareness — you catch the runaway bill in the dashboard, not the invoice; efficiency is part of the job. 
Ephemeral environments — spin up a full stack per PR/demo, tear it down after. 
A debugger of infrastructure — reads the deploy log, the metric spike, the routing table, and sees it.

AI-native. You work with AI on all levels — you understand the technology around you (LLMs, SLMs, RAG, knowledge graphs, agents, training, eval) and you use AI tools daily to exponentially increase your velocity. 
Distributed-systems literate. High-efficiency, event-driven, low-latency systems are our world; you understand what that demands. 
Innovators who ship. You demonstrate ideas easily, fail fast, and move forward. You make committed timelines and hit them. 
You consider yourself exceptional — and you like winning. So do we. 
No one will have everything in this description. We're looking for well-rounded, smart people who move fast.
What You Will Do:
The role:
The technical face to enterprise customers — scoping deployments, designing tenant configurations, and getting customers live fast (same-day with Desktop Intercept). 
You're selling and deploying a platform that combines voice, desktop, intelligence, and AI — technology that changes monthly — so you learn constantly and demo fearlessly.
Startup environment: the deal, the deployment, and the product are all moving at once, and you thrive in that. 
What you'll own:
Pre-sales and deployment architecture
Tenant configuration and plugin enablement design
Customer integration scoping (CCaaS / CRM / SIP) · live demos that win — show-me applies to customers too 
The customer's voice back into Product and Engineering
Your committed go-live timelines. 
Who you are:
A self-starter with grit and a closer's instinct — you like winning, and a signed customer going live is your scoreboard.
Show-me mentality: you'd rather run the live demo than present the slide.
You adapt fast when the product shifts under you (it will, weekly), love new technology, and use AI tools daily — including in your own demo and scoping workflow.
A do-er who owns the messy middle instead of escalating it.
A team player who translates in both directions: business requirements into technical needs for engineering, platform capability into business value for the customer. 
What You Will Bring:
8+ years of solutions architecture/sales engineering in contact-center, CCaaS, or enterprise SaaS. 
Technical enough to design an integration on a whiteboard and credible enough to own a CTO conversation — you keep the respect of senior engineers on both sides of the table. 
Knows CCaaS / CTI, SIP / RTP, and CRM landscapes cold. 
Strong working knowledge of the modern AI stack — LLMs, RAG, knowledge graphs, agents, transcription/translation — deep enough to answer the customer's AI architecture and data-security questions without phoning home. 
Has taken enterprise customers live and owned the messy middle — network quirks, security reviews, procurement, the works. 
Hands-on enough to configure a tenant, read an API payload, and debug a customer integration in real time — a troubleshooter, not a talker: when the pilot breaks at 4pm, you isolate it. 
Understands event-driven platform architecture well enough to scope custom integrations accurately — what's config, what's a connector, what's a feature request. 
Deployment playbook craft — turns every go-live into a repeatable playbook so the second customer is faster than the first; this is how one SA scales. 
Enterprise security fluency — comfortable in InfoSec reviews (SOC 2, data residency, PII/redaction, AI data-usage questions); AI deals die here without it. 
Competitive positioning depth — knows the CCaaS/agent-assist landscape and can architect around a competitor's incumbency. 
POC discipline — scopes pilots with clear success criteria and exit dates, so pilots convert instead of drifting.

title: Software Engineer III (Bangalore, India)
content:
ABOUT AIPRISE

AiPrise is a global compliance orchestration platform helping fintechs, marketplaces, and payment companies verify and onboard customers worldwide. We integrate with 80+ identity and compliance vendors to deliver a holistic view of risk. We're now building AI-powered compliance agents to revolutionize KYB, AML, sanctions screening, and risk scoring — enabling our customers to onboard faster, reduce manual reviews, and prevent financial crime.




ROLE OVERVIEW

We’re hiring a Software Engineer II to help build and scale the core platform behind AiPrise’s compliance orchestration and AI agent systems.

This is a build it, ship it, own it role. You’ll take features end to end, from design to code to deploy to iterate, across our case management product, vendor integrations, orchestration APIs, and customer facing tools. You’ll be in the trenches with founders and a fast moving team, turning messy real world compliance problems into clean, reliable systems. If you’re a hungry engineer who wants real ownership, high impact, and a product that gets used in production every day, you’ll love this.




WHAT YOU'LL DO




BUILD & OWN FEATURES END-TO-END

 - Design, develop, and ship production features across our platform stack (backend APIs, data pipelines, integrations, case management UI)

 - Own complete features from requirements gathering → implementation → deployment → monitoring

 - Build scalable REST APIs and microservices that orchestrate checks across 80+ compliance vendors (identity verification, sanctions screening, document analysis)

 - Develop case management workflows and business logic for KYB/AML compliance processes

 - Create data pipelines for ingesting, transforming, and routing compliance data at scale

 - Integrate with third-party identity/compliance APIs and handle complex vendor response mapping




DRIVE TECHNICAL EXCELLENCE

 - Write clean, maintainable, well-tested code with comprehensive documentation

 - Participate in code reviews and contribute to engineering best practices

 - Debug production issues with urgency; own incident resolution end-to-end

 - Optimize system performance, reliability, and cost-efficiency

 - Build monitoring, alerting, and observability into your features


COLLABORATE

 - Work cross-functionally with product managers, compliance experts, and customer success teams

 - Contribute to technical decision-making and architecture discussions

 - Help shape engineering culture and development workflows as the team scales




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR




MUST-HAVE:

 - 4-7+ years of professional software engineering experience building and shipping production systems

 - Strong programming fundamentals in at least one modern backend language (Python, Go, Java, Node.js, or similar)

 - Experience building RESTful APIs, microservices, or distributed systems

 - Solid understanding of relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL) and data modeling

 - Hands-on experience with cloud platforms (AWS preferred, GCP/Azure acceptable)

 - Familiarity with Git, CI/CD pipelines, Docker, and modern deployment practices

 - Proven ability to own features end-to-end — you've taken projects from ambiguous requirements through production launch

 - Strong debugging and problem-solving skills; comfortable working in unfamiliar codebases

 - Excellent communication skills and ability to translate business needs into technical solutions

 - Experience mentoring or supporting junior engineers (formal or informal)




NICE-TO-HAVE:

 - Experience in FinTech, RegTech, payments, or fraud/risk detection domains

 - Knowledge of compliance workflows (KYC/KYB, AML, sanctions screening, adverse media)

 - Experience with event-driven architectures and message queues (Kafka, RabbitMQ, AWS SQS)

 - Familiarity with NoSQL databases (MongoDB, DynamoDB) or search engines (Elasticsearch)

 - Experience integrating with third-party APIs and managing vendor relationships at scale

 - Frontend development experience (React, TypeScript) for building internal tools

 - Background working with ML/AI systems or data-intensive applications

 - Kubernetes, Terraform, or infrastructure-as-code experience




SUCCESS IN THIS ROLE LOOKS LIKE

 - In 3 Months: You've shipped 2-3 significant features to production, own key platform components (e.g., vendor orchestration layer, case management API), and are actively mentoring a junior engineer through onboarding and feature development

 - In 9 Months: You're a go-to expert for critical platform areas, driving technical decisions for major initiatives, leading cross-functional feature teams, and have measurably improved engineering velocity and code quality. You've reduced manual review time for customers and helped scale the platform to handle 2-3 enterprise clients.




WHY AIPRISE

 - Build mission-critical software that directly fights financial crime and fraud for companies like Meta and leading fintechs

 - Work with diverse, complex datasets from 200+ countries

 - Join a fast-moving YC-backed startup where your work has immediate customer impact

 - Ship quickly — your code will reach production in days, not months

 - Collaborate in-person with a talented, mission-driven team in San Jose

 - Competitive compensation with meaningful equity upside

 


ABOUT THE INTERVIEW

 1. Remote: Exploratory Discussion

 2. In-office
    
    1. DSA/Problem Solving 1 
    
    2. DSA/Problem Solving 2
    
    3. System Design Interview

 3. Remote: Behavioural (Head of Engineering)

title: Product Designer II
content:
ABOUT AIPRISE

AiPrise is a YC-backed, Series A company building the global compliance infrastructure for financial services. We help banks, fintechs, cross-border payment providers, stablecoin and crypto companies, and marketplaces gain a 360° view of every business they onboard, anywhere in the world.



Through a single integration, we connect 800+ data sources and 80+ verification partners across 200+ countries, powering KYB, KYC, AML, sanctions screening, and ongoing monitoring for companies like Meta, Airwallex, Fireblocks, and Bridge.



Our AI Agents help compliance teams do more with less, resolving more cases, catching more fraud, and scaling operations without scaling headcount.



We're ~60 people, Series A funded, and obsessed with a single problem: making compliance feel simple for the teams who live in it every day.



Borders shouldn't be blockers. Compliance is hard. AiPrise shouldn't be.



 
 


THE ROLE

As a Product Designer II at AiPrise, you'll own design for a defined feature area of our compliance platform end to end, turning complicated processes, data, and decisions into clear, intuitive experiences.



Our platform serves compliance analysts reviewing flagged cases, compliance managers configuring the rules that decide what gets flagged, business customers completing verification for the first time, and our own Forward-Deployed Engineering team standing up and supporting customer workflows. Depending on where you're working, you'll design for several of them.



You'll work with product and engineering to take defined problems from discovery through launch. The problem and its owner will be clear; how it gets solved is where you come in. We move fast and share work early, so expect feedback from customers and teammates to shape your designs while they're still taking form.



You'll partner closely with product and engineering, with enough proximity to leadership to see why decisions get made and how your work lands with customers. Our priorities and processes will keep evolving as we grow, so you'll prioritize your own work with limited oversight and change course when new information arrives.



 
 


WHAT YOU'LL DO


DESIGN JUDGMENT

 - Make design decisions independently within your feature area, applying and extending our design system where it needs to stretch.

 - Weigh user needs, design quality, delivery speed, business priorities, and technical constraints, and catch usability problems before they reach engineering.

 - Build working domain expertise in the compliance and verification workflows your feature area touches, deep enough to connect your day-to-day design work to roadmap goals and explain how it ladders up to quarterly objectives.


EXECUTION

 - Own medium-complexity projects end to end, from discovery and exploration through final design, implementation, and launch, with minimal oversight.

 - Create clear user flows, prototypes, final designs, and documentation, anticipating edge cases and the non-happy paths that make compliance software either trustworthy or infuriating.


CUSTOMER & DATA INSIGHTS

 - Combine customer conversations, usability testing, and product analytics to validate design decisions and identify problems worth solving, rather than only responding to the feedback in front of you.

 - Work with internal teams who sit closest to customers to pressure-test what you're seeing in the data.


COMMUNICATION & INFLUENCE

 - Partner closely with product and engineering to clarify the problem, requirements, constraints, and measures of success.

 - Explain your design rationale clearly, contribute confidently in product and planning discussions, and keep stakeholders current on progress, risks, and open questions.

 - Help newer designers get better, through design reviews, feedback, and pairing on tricky problems.

 
 


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3+ years as a product designer, with a track record of shipping features and workflows to customers.

 - Experience designing complex B2B, enterprise, fintech, compliance, identity, fraud, risk, or other data-heavy products, where the hard part was the information and not the interface.

 - A portfolio that shows how you frame problems, use research and data, explore solutions, and make design decisions, not just the final screens.

 - Fluency in interaction design, information architecture, visual design, and prototyping, with the attention to edge cases and implementation quality that complex products demand.

 - Clear written and verbal communication, and a collaborative approach to working with product managers and engineers.

ROLE OVERVIEW

We're hiring a Staff Software Engineer in Bangalore to set the technical direction for the core platform behind AiPrise's compliance orchestration and AI agent systems.

This is our most senior individual-contributor role. You will own the architecture of a major part of the platform, lead the hardest multi-quarter technical initiatives across teams, and raise the engineering bar for a team that is growing fast. You'll work directly with the head of engineering, engineering managers, product managers, FDEs, etc. to turn customer and regulatory needs into technical strategy, and then ship it.

We process verification requests for financial institutions in a regulated environment, so reliability, security, and data integrity are not afterthoughts. If you want a role where your judgment shapes how the platform scales for the next several years, and where you still write code, this is it.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO


SET TECHNICAL DIRECTION

 - Own the architecture and multi-quarter technical roadmap for a core area of the platform: vendor orchestration, case management, platform, or the AI agents

 - Lead our largest and most ambiguous technical initiatives end to end: framing the problem, design, sequencing across teams, delivery, and rollout or migration

 - Author and review RFCs, run design reviews, and make the hard calls on build vs. buy, consistency vs. speed, and when to pay down debt

 - Set the standard for reliability, security, and data integrity in a regulated environment: SLOs, incident response, change management, and audit-readiness


SCALE THE PLATFORM

 - Evolve the orchestration layer to handle 10x verification volume across 80+ vendors: throughput, latency, failover, and cost

 - Shape the developer platform (service boundaries, shared libraries, CI/CD, observability) so a fast-growing team can ship safely and often

 - Take our AI agent systems from promising to production-grade: evaluation, guardrails, human-in-the-loop workflows, and the data pipelines behind them

 - Stay hands-on: prototype the risky parts, unblock critical paths, and ship code that others build on


MULTIPLY THE TEAM

 - Act as technical lead and mentor to senior engineers; grow the next generation of tech leads

 - Partner with the founders, engineering managers, product, and compliance experts on the roadmap; translate customer and regulatory needs into technical strategy

 - Represent engineering with enterprise customers on architecture, security reviews, and integration design

 - Help us hire: design interviews, calibrate the bar, and close senior candidates




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR


MUST-HAVE

 - 9+ years building and operating production systems, with at least 2 years at Staff-level scope: setting technical direction for multiple teams or a major system

 - A track record of leading cross-team technical initiatives from an ambiguous problem to a shipped, adopted result

 - Deep expertise in distributed systems and backend architecture: service design, data modeling, API design, event-driven systems, consistency trade-offs, and failure modes

 - You have designed, scaled, and operated high-throughput, high-reliability systems, and carried the pager for them

 - Strong in at least one of Python, Go, or TypeScript/Node.js; comfortable working across the stack when the problem calls for it

 - Writing that changes decisions: RFCs, design docs, and postmortems that a team can act on

 - Experience mentoring senior engineers and measurably raising an organization's engineering standards

 - Judgment about when to be pragmatic and when to insist, and the credibility to carry either call with founders and peers


NICE-TO-HAVE

 - Experience in FinTech, RegTech, payments, identity verification, or fraud/risk detection, and working knowledge of KYC/KYB, AML, and sanctions screening

 - Built or operated a platform that integrates dozens of third-party vendors: response normalization, failover, rate limits, and vendor observability

 - Shipped production LLM or ML systems: evaluation, guardrails, cost and latency management, document intelligence

 - Security and compliance engineering: SOC 2 or ISO 27001, data residency, encryption, audit trails

 - Helped an engineering team grow several-fold while keeping quality and velocity up

 - Frontend experience (React, TypeScript) for internal tools and case management UI


SUCCESS IN THIS ROLE LOOKS LIKE

 - In 1 month: You understand the platform end to end, have shipped a meaningful improvement to a critical path, and have published an RFC with a clear point of view on our highest-leverage technical problem. You've taken on technical leadership of a core area.

 - In 3 months: You're leading a cross-team initiative with a defined roadmap and visible progress. Design reviews and RFCs are a working habit across the team, not a ritual. At least one reliability or velocity metric has moved because of your work.

 - In 3 months: The architecture for the platform's next phase is defined and delivered. Senior engineers you've mentored are leading their own initiatives. The founders and engineering managers treat you as the technical counterpart for the hardest calls.


WHY AIPRISE

title: HR Manager - Bangalore
content:
ABOUT AIPRISE

AiPrise is a YC-backed, Series A company building the global compliance infrastructure for financial services. We help banks, fintechs, cross-border payment providers, stablecoin and crypto companies, and marketplaces get a 360° view of every business they onboard, anywhere in the world.

Through a single integration, we connect 800+ data sources and 80+ verification partners across 200+ countries, powering KYB, KYC, AML, sanctions screening, and ongoing monitoring for companies like Meta, Airwallex, Fireblocks, and Bridge. Our AI Agents help compliance teams resolve more cases, catch more fraud, and scale without scaling headcount.

We're about 60 people across San Jose and Bangalore, and growing fast. Borders shouldn't be blockers.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring our first HR Manager in India to own people operations and the workplace for our Bangalore team. You'll be the senior people leader on the ground: the person employees, managers, and candidates trust to get things right.

This is a builder role. You'll run India payroll with our vendor, keep us compliant with Indian labour law, lead onboarding and recruiting, and shape our next Bangalore office from the ground up. You'll partner closely with our US HR Manager and India leadership, and you'll have real ownership, not just tasks.

The role is in office 4 days a week at HSR Layout. Being present matters here: you'll be the face of HR and the office for a team that's growing quickly.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

HR operations and compliance

 - Own HR for AiPrise India Private Limited: policies, employee records, letters, and the full employee lifecycle

 - Keep us compliant with Indian labour law, including the four Labour Codes and Karnataka state rules, Shops and Establishments registration, and statutory registers

 - Run our POSH program: Internal Committee, annual training, and required filings

 - Be the go-to advisor for managers on performance, employee relations, and sensitive conversations, and lead investigations and exits with care

 - Maintain clean data in Rippling (our HRIS) and support audit and SOC 2 evidence requests

Payroll and benefits

 - Manage monthly India payroll with our payroll vendor: inputs, joiners and leavers, variable pay, reimbursements, and final settlements

 - Review payroll outputs for accuracy before approval and resolve employee pay questions quickly

 - Own statutory compliance in partnership with the vendor: PF, ESI, Professional Tax, TDS, gratuity, and timely filings

 - Administer India benefits such as group health insurance, and help employees understand them

Onboarding and recruiting

 - Own onboarding for every Bangalore hire, from offer acceptance and background checks through day one and the first 90 days

 - Partner with hiring managers to plan headcount, run interview processes, and keep a great candidate experience

 - Manage candidates and pipeline in Ashby, prepare offer letters, and keep offers consistent and confidential

 - Coordinate with recruiting agencies and build our employer brand in Bangalore

Office build-out and facilities

 - Lead our move into a new Bangalore office: space planning, vendor selection, fit-out timelines, budget tracking, and move day

 - Own day-to-day office operations: building management, maintenance, access, IT equipment logistics, and supplies

 - Manage facilities vendors (cleaning, pantry, courier, security) and their contracts and spend

 - Plan in-office culture: team events, visits from the US team, and offsite logistics
   
   
   
   
   WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
   
   Must haves
   
   - 6 to 10 years in HR, including 2+ years as the HR lead or generalist for an India entity
   
   - Hands-on India payroll experience working with a payroll vendor, including statutory compliance (PF, ESI, PT, TDS, gratuity)
   
   - Working knowledge of Indian labour law and the Labour Codes, POSH, and Karnataka requirements
   
   - Experience owning onboarding and supporting recruiting at a growing company
   
   - Experience running office or facilities operations, ideally including an office setup or move
   
   - Sound judgment and discretion with confidential information like compensation and employee relations matters
   
   - Clear, confident communication with employees, leaders, and a manager based in the US
   
   - Able to be in our HSR Layout office 4 days a week
   
   Nice to haves
   
   - Experience at a startup or high-growth tech company working with a global team
   
   - Experience with Rippling, Ashby, or similar HRIS and ATS tools
   
   - Background supporting SOC 2 or similar audits
   
   - MBA or PG degree in HR, or a related qualification

title: AI Native Builder/Architect
content:
WHO WE ARE

Atlan is building the context layer for enterprise AI. Enterprises are pouring money into AI and most of it dies in production because the AI does not understand the business context around the data. That is the problem Atlan solves.

Gartner has named context the defining issue in enterprise AI, and calls context graphs the essential infrastructure for AI agents, naming Atlan one of three vendors already building it. We are also the only vendor named a Leader across all four major Gartner and Forrester evaluations for data catalogs, data governance and metadata management, the foundation the context layer runs on.

Come build the infrastructure that AI runs on.


WHO WE ARE

Gartner calls context the defining issue in enterprise AI, and context graphs the essential infrastructure for AI agents. It names Atlan as one of three vendors already building one. We're also the only vendor named a Leader in all four major Gartner and Forrester evaluations for data catalogs, data governance and metadata management, the layer our context graph is built on.

Come build the infrastructure AI runs on.



THE TEAM

You'll join the team building Atlan's context layer, the platforms that make it possible and the vertical agents that run on it. The platform is what any agent needs before an enterprise will trust it: a registry of which agents and skills exist, traces and evals on every run, and governance over cost and access.

Vertical agents each do one specific job, for customers and for Atlan's own teams. Inside Atlan they already run real work. There's an agent our CSMs trust, three GTM agents that replace 3,000 calls made by hand, an agent that watches every page on atlan.com http://atlan.com, and one that monitors the other agents. We write up what we learn in the open at Becoming Frontier https://atlan.com/frontier/.

The team works in small "two-slice" units. You own one initiative, usually with one or two people alongside you, and you decide how it gets built.



WHAT WILL YOU DO?

You'll take problems nobody has fully defined yet and ship working systems, fast. Depending on where you're matched, you may:

 - Own a 0→1 initiative from problem to production. Frame it, write the spec when there isn't one, pick the architecture and build it.

 - Build agents with the people who own the outcome, inside Atlan or at a customer. Scope the workflow with them, demo early and put the agent where the work already happens, like an approval in Slack or a redline in a legal team's Word doc.

 - Earn autonomy with evidence. Start with shadow runs, study the misses and widen what the agent can do as results support it.

 - Design for failure. Decide what happens when a tool is down, context is thin or the agent isn't sure, and how a person takes over.

 - Make the engineering calls on what stays deterministic code and what needs a model, build vs. reuse, model choice, cost and reliability. Explain the trade-offs clearly.

 - Make agent behavior observable. Tie traces and evals to the revision that ran. Track consistency, cost and latency alongside success rate, and treat drift as a regression.

 - Build on and extend the context layer, agent platform and registry: versioned skills, layered instructions, explicit permissions for tools and secrets, and model changes handled as migrations with evals rerun before promotion.

 - Build AI-native yourself. Run coding agents on your own work, keep their skills and instructions up to date, and review what they write for architectural drift.

 - Share what you learn. Turn what works into skills, reference architectures and quality gates that others adopt, and demo what you've built.


WHAT MAKES YOU A GREAT MATCH FOR US?


MUST HAVE

 - You've built software systems hands-on and shipped 0→1 products or platforms into production, often without a spec.

 - You've shipped agents or LLM systems that real people use. When one went wrong, you traced it back to the context, tool call or decision that caused it.

 - You use evals to find and fix real problems, check what a score actually counts, and judge agents by user impact: hours saved, error rate or cycle time.

 - You design for failure first: what the agent may touch, what happens when it's wrong, and where a person approves before it acts.

 - You build with coding agents every day and hold what they write to the same bar as your own code.

 - You're a critical optimist. You believe what agents can do is real, and test what still fails before trusting them with more.

 - You reason from first principles. When a familiar design doesn't fit, or a better model makes old scaffolding unnecessary, you notice and rebuild.

 - You have strong systems judgment. You can design for production reliability, latency, cost and security, build it yourself, and leave it in a shape others can build on.

 - You do your best work owning an initiative with one or two people alongside you, and don't need a large team to feel effective.


STRONG BONUS

 - Experience with MCP, A2A, agent frameworks and runtimes, LLM gateways or agent observability, or you've built an agent harness or orchestration layer yourself.

 - Experience with knowledge graphs, vector search, retrieval or semantic layers.

 - You've built an eval suite from scratch, or run shadow evaluations, LLM grading or staged rollouts.

 - You've shipped agents that write to a system of record, with permissions, approvals and an audit trail.

 - You've led AI adoption inside an engineering or business team and can show the before and after.

 - Founding-engineer, technical-founder or early-stage startup experience, where you built something from nothing.

 - A public trail of work, repos, demos, write-ups or talks, that shows how you build.

title: Social Media Manager
content:
ABOUT ATLYS

Our mission is to enable every person on Earth to travel freely.

Travel should feel exciting. Instead, too much of it is still defined by paperwork, uncertainty, and processes that were never designed for travellers.

Atlys http://atlys.com/ is changing that.

We’re building an AI-first platform that removes friction and uncertainty from travel. To date, we’ve processed visas for 1M+ travellers across 127 countries. But we’re still early.

 


THE ROLE

We're looking for a Social Media Manager who understands how to build a brand people want to follow, engage with, and share.

You'll own Atlys' social media presence across relevant platforms, from developing the content strategy and identifying trends to driving execution and analysing performance. You'll work at the intersection of culture, creativity, and growth, translating travel insights, internet trends, creator content, and audience conversations into compelling social-first storytelling.

We're looking for someone who can develop strong creative ideas, recognise what will resonate with an audience, and build a social presence that contributes to brand awareness, community engagement, and business growth.




THE JOB

 - Own social media strategy: Develop and execute a platform-specific social media strategy aligned with Atlys' brand positioning, marketing priorities, and growth objectives.

 - Drive content ideation: Generate creative concepts, recurring content series, campaign ideas, and social-first formats that make Atlys relevant to travellers.

 - Manage content execution: Own the social media calendar, coordinate briefs and production, manage publishing schedules, and ensure consistent execution across channels.

 - Stay ahead of trends: Identify emerging formats, cultural moments, internet conversations, and travel trends that Atlys can participate in authentically.

 - Build a distinctive brand voice: Develop a recognisable tone of voice and ensure consistency across posts, comments, captions, and other social touchpoints.

 - Collaborate with creators: Work with influencers, content creators, and internal creative teams to develop content that feels native to each platform.

 - Build community: Engage with followers, respond to relevant conversations, identify audience insights, and develop initiatives that encourage participation and sharing.

 - Partner with Growth and Creative: Collaborate on campaigns, launches, and paid-social initiatives, ensuring that learnings from organic content inform broader creative and marketing strategies.

 - Track and optimise performance: Monitor reach, engagement, shares, saves, follower growth, watch time, and other relevant metrics to identify what works and why.

 - Experiment continuously: Test new formats, hooks, content pillars, and storytelling approaches to improve content performance and strengthen Atlys' social presence.



THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

You’ll likely thrive in this role if you:

 - 3–6 years of experience in social media management, social content strategy, or digital marketing.

 - Hands-on experience managing brand accounts across platforms such as Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn, and other relevant social channels.

 - A strong understanding of short-form video, social-first storytelling, platform-specific content formats, and audience behaviour.

 - Excellent creative judgement and the ability to identify trends worth pursuing rather than simply replicating what is popular.

 - Experience building content calendars, briefing creatives, coordinating production, and managing end-to-end execution.

 - A strong understanding of social media analytics and the ability to translate performance data into actionable insights.

 - Excellent communication, copywriting, and stakeholder management skills.

 - The ability to balance creative experimentation with consistent execution in a fast-paced environment.

 - Familiarity with social media analytics, publishing tools, video editing workflows, and AI-powered content tools.

We hire exceptional people for their craft, not travel enthusiasts. We solve hard problems that happen to touch global travel and government infrastructure.

 


WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT

Atlys is built by a small team with outsized ambition, high ownership, and an obsession with doing great work.

Here’s what you can expect:

 - Competitive compensation and equity so you participate in the value you help create.

 - Comprehensive health insurance covering you and your family, plus annual preventive health check-up on us.

 - A thoughtful leave policy with paid time off and company holidays, because great work also requires real time off.

 - Lunch, high tea and dinner at the office, so the basics are taken care of while we build together.

 - Learning & development credits to invest in courses, books, conferences and tools that help you get better at your craft.

 - Relocation support to make moving closer to the team as seamless as possible.

 - Great tools to do your best work, including high-spec equipment and software.

 - An office designed for more than just work, with pickleball, table tennis, PlayStation, an arcade game room, an F1 simulator and even a full flight simulator.
   
    

Our values shape how we make decisions, work together and build for travelers. The bar is high, the pace is fast, and the way we work is deliberate. Read them before you apply. If this environment energizes you, you’ll probably thrive here. If it doesn’t, it’s better to know that upfront.

title: Platform & Security Engineer
content:
ABOUT ATLYS

Our mission is to enable every person on Earth to travel freely.

Travel should feel exciting. Instead, too much of it is still defined by paperwork, uncertainty, and processes that were never designed for travellers.

Atlys is changing that.

We're building an AI-first platform that removes friction and uncertainty from travel. To date, we've processed visas for 1M+ travellers across 127 countries. But we're still early. We’re now building AI-native products too, including agents that act on behalf of travellers.


THE ROLE

We're looking for a Platform & Security Engineer to own the foundations that keep Atlys fast, reliable and secure.

Not someone who simply keeps servers running or closes tickets from a scanner. We're looking for someone who treats infrastructure and security as products: who designs systems that are secure by default, automates away toil, and gives every engineer a paved road to ship safely.

Few companies handle data as sensitive as ours. Passports, financial documents, photographs and identity records flow every day between travellers, partners and government systems across 127 countries. You'll own the cloud infrastructure, security posture and reliability of the platform that processes it, and make sure it scales as we grow.

You’ll be the second engineer on our Infra & Security team. That means real ownership from week one: you’ll take over large parts of our infrastructure and security roadmap, not a narrow slice of it.

We don’t expect you to have done all of this before. We care far more about strong fundamentals and the ability to figure things out. You’ll have AI tools at your disposal and the room to learn whatever you haven’t touched yet.


THE JOB

 - Own our cloud infrastructure. Run and improve our Kubernetes platform on GCP (with some workloads on AWS). Make deployments repeatable and fast with multi-stage CI/CD, container promotion and GitOps.

 - Make the platform observable and reliable. Bring logs, metrics and traces into one place, set up alerting that people trust, and take part in on-call and incident response. Keep an eye on cloud cost and catch anomalies early.

 - Run our data layer. Own database performance optimizations, backups and access automation, along with caching and our messaging infrastructure.

 - Lock down access. Enforce least-privilege IAM across cloud, Kubernetes and GitHub. Run zero-trust access to internal services, SSO, and clean offboarding.

 - Protect sensitive data. Design and harden access controls and audit logging for PII such as passports, financial documents and identity records.

 - Build security into how we ship. Add SAST, DAST, dependency and container scanning, and SBOMs to CI/CD. Run vulnerability management and coordinate pentests. Find and validate application security issues (authorization, authentication, business logic, injection), drive fixes with service owners, and fix directly where it makes sense.

 - Secure our AI products. Threat-model and harden AI agents and assistants that act on users’ behalf: prompt injection, tool and OAuth scope permissions, data leakage between users, and secrets handling.


THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

You'll likely thrive in this role if you:

 - Have 4+ years of experience in infrastructure, DevOps, security engineering, ideally at a product company handling sensitive or regulated data.

 - Have strong fundamentals in Linux, networking (DNS, TLS, HTTP, load balancing), containers and Kubernetes, and at least one public cloud.

 - Understand security fundamentals (identity and access, encryption, secrets management, the OWASP Top 10) and have applied them in production, not just on paper.

 - Are strong in either infrastructure or security, and genuinely want to get good at the other.

 - Take ownership end to end. You make pragmatic trade-offs between security, speed and developer experience. You explain risk clearly and bring engineers along rather than acting as a gatekeeper.

 - Can write code to automate your way out of problems (Python, Go or Bash), and are comfortable reading application code.

 - Figure things out. When you hit something new, you read the docs, use AI tools well, test your assumptions and ship.

Nice-to-Have:

 - Prior web or backend development experience

 - Exposure to compliance frameworks such as DPDPA, ISO 27001 or SOC 2

 - Experience securing LLM applications or AI agents

You will own the infrastructure that our next family of foundational models is trained on. This is a deep systems role: distributed training at scale, parallelism strategies, GPU kernel work, throughput and stability optimization, and the unglamorous reliability engineering that determines whether a frontier training run actually finishes.

The bar is high. A bad MFU number, a slow data loader, a switch flap — these are problems whose cost is measured in weeks and millions of dollars. You will be expected to find them before they happen, and to fix them fast when they do.

What You’ll Do

 - Build, maintain, and continually push the limits of our distributed training stack across large GPU clusters.

 - Design and implement parallelism strategies — data, tensor, pipeline, sequence, expert — and reason about which combinations make sense for which architectures and which scales.

 - Profile and optimize end-to-end training throughput: kernel performance, communication overlap, memory layout, checkpointing, data loading.

 - Write and tune custom GPU kernels (CUDA, Triton) where off-the-shelf is leaving performance on the table.

 - Own the reliability of long-running training jobs — fault tolerance, checkpoint integrity, deterministic restarts, automated detection of slow nodes and silent corruption.

 - Partner closely with researchers to make sure architectural ideas can actually be trained efficiently, and with the data team to keep the pipeline from being the bottleneck.



What We’re Looking For

 - BS or MS in Computer Science or a closely related technical field (or equivalent demonstrated experience).

 - 3+ years of experience building ML training infrastructure or large-scale distributed systems. Exceptional early-career candidates with a strong systems background will be considered.

 - Hands-on experience training large models with distributed training frameworks — Megatron-LM, DeepSpeed, FSDP, NeMo, or equivalent. You should have been on-call for a real pretraining run.

 - Deep working knowledge of GPU architecture, the CUDA programming model, and standard tools for profiling GPU workloads (Nsight, PyTorch profiler, etc.).

 - Strong PyTorch internals knowledge. You're comfortable reading and modifying low-level training code, not just using high-level APIs.

 - Meaningful open-source contributions in the training infrastructure ecosystem — Megatron, DeepSpeed, PyTorch, vLLM, Triton, NCCL, or similar.

Bonus Points

content:
About Sarvam

Sarvam is building the bedrock of Sovereign AI for India.
